request.spec:
A steward can move a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claim to another person on the sheet (a refusal shows an
error on the claim). The claim keeps its number and date, loses any figure a statement bound it to
(it is live again until its new person's next statement), every total follows, and CLAIM_REASSIGNED
is written, naming the claim like every claim line (with the new person) and ending from=<old name>
to=<new name>. A settled or voided claim cannot move. The moved claim is listed as its new person's
newest claim (first under them), whatever its date.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can move a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claim to another person on the sheet (a refusal shows an
error on the claim). The claim keeps its number and date, loses any figure a statement bound it to
(it is live again until its new person's next statement), every total follows, and CLAIM_REASSIGNED
is written, naming the claim like every claim line (with the new person) and ending from=<old name>
to=<new name>. A settled or voided claim cannot move. The moved claim is listed as its new person's
newest claim (first under them), whatever its date.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A steward can now move a claim to another person on the sheet, and all 4 tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

**How it behaves**
- Only a steward can move a claim, and only a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING one. Anything else is refused and shows `claim-error` on the claim row, writing nothing. That covers a non-steward, a settled or voided claim, an unknown person, and moving a claim to the person who already has it.
- The claim keeps its number and date. Any figure a statement bound it to is cleared, so its due is worked out fresh at the new person's rate until their next statement.
- The audit line is `CLAIM_REASSIGNED … person=<new> amount=… date=… [number=…] from=<old> to=<new>`. After it come the usual `ROLLUP`/`TOTALS` lines for whatever totals changed; moving a draft changes none, so it writes only the one line.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** the migration `V25__claim_listed.sql` adds a `listed_seq` column to claims, and claims are now listed newest first by that column instead of by id. New and moved claims get the next value, which is how a moved claim ends up first under its new person whatever its date.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/reassign`, wired in `reassign.POST.yml` like the existing status endpoint. It uses new classes `ValidateReassign`, `ApplyReassign`, `SaveReassign` and `AuditClaimReassigned`, plus `Claims.reassign` in the store.
- **Front end:** each claim row in `ClaimList.tsx` has a person dropdown (`claim-reassign-to`) and a reassign button (`claim-reassign`). The dropdown lists everyone except the claim's current person. `PeopleList` passes the people list into it.

**Choices the request didn't cover:**
- Moving a claim whose date falls in a closed period is allowed. Status changes in a closed period are refused, but reassigning isn't.
- Retired or held people can be chosen as the new person.
- Two claims moved or added at exactly the same moment could get the same list position. Ties fall back to id order, so the list still shows, but which comes first between those two may not be exact.
